OpenStudio-HPXML assigns the fraction of the duct area in the conditioned space if the duct location is in unconditioned space. If the number of floors above grade is greater than one, then 25% of the duct surface area is assigned to the conditioned space. OpenStudio-HPXML also assigns fractions of supply/return ducts with rectangular and circular cross-sections, which affects the effective R-value for a given nominal duct insulation R-value. 3.1 OpenStudio-HPXML Overview The ResStock building stock energy model includes conditional probability distributions of building characteristics that represent the contiguous U.S. residential building stock. These distributions are sampled to create a synthetic stock, with each sample assigned an option for each characteristic for every dwelling unit to be simulated. ResStock utilizes the OpenStudio- HPXML workflow to translate these dwelling characteristics into building models that can be simulated with OpenStudio® and EnergyPlus® using an HPXML file. For reference, the state of the OpenStudio-HPXML repository when the ResStock 2025 Release 1 dataset was created can be found here. 3.2 Duct Sealing and Insulation Upgrades Each building characteristic assigned in ResStock is translated to OS-HPXML parameters via a file called options_lookup.tsv. A measure upgrade is modeled as changes to specific building characteristics of a model defined using the baseline building stock characteristics. This section covers the technical details of the duct sealing and insulation upgrade changes in the ResStock workflow.
